Half-width of the peer-reliability band in .gloc_cond_resid

Source: R/cellgloc_utils.R
dot-gloc_peer_band.Rd

The peer-inclusion rule \(w > w_{\min}\) is applied over a band \([w_{\min} - h, w_{\min} + h]\) rather than at a point, which is what makes the soft corner's weight map continuous; see the "peer band" section of .gloc_cond_resid for the argument and the construction.

.gloc_peer_band

Format

a length-one numeric.

Details

The value is a compromise between two measurable things. Too narrow and the map is continuous but so steep that the relaxed iteration still overshoots: the damped update \(w \mapsto (1 - d) w + d f(w)\) is locally contracting only while \(f' > 1 - 2/d\), and \(f'\) across the band is about \(-\Delta / 2h\) where \(\Delta \approx 0.2\) is the measured jump a single threshold crossing used to produce, so \(h\) must exceed about \(\Delta d / 2\) – 0.025 at an unrelaxed step and less when relaxed. Too wide and the interpolation stops being a fringe: bisquare weights sit at 0.5 at \(|z| = 2.55\), so a band of \(\pm h\) covers the standardised residuals in roughly \(|z| \in (2.55 - 4h, 2.55 + 4h)\), which at \(h = 0.05\) is about 1.2% of clean Gaussian cells and at \(h = 0.25\) would be nearer 10%.

0.05 sits above the steepness bound and below the fringe bound. Measured on a sweep of one cell's weight across the threshold (the portable test data, drawn as Z %*% chol(S)), the largest one-step jump it leaves in a row-mate's standardised residual is 0.0071, against 0.225 for the hard cut, a factor of 32, with identical values outside the band. (Corrected: this page quoted 0.0035 against 0.110, figures that matched neither the earlier MASS::mvrnorm test data nor the current ones.)
